title: An 8-week study plan
lines: Eight weeks is a comfortable length for most test takers. It gives you time to learn every topic once, practice your weak areas properly and build stamina with regular full mocks. Plan on about 1.5 hours on weekdays and 3 hours on one weekend day, roughly 80-90 hours in total.
## Principles
- Two phases: weeks 1-4 build skills topic by topic; weeks 5-8 turn them into test performance.
- Vocabulary every day, 15-20 minutes.
- One full mock test every week or two, more often near the end.
- One timed essay every week.
! Keep a short error log from the first week: question, topic, why you missed it (concept, careless, timing, vocabulary). It will guide every later week.
## Before you start
- Read the articles in "The exam" group.
- Take Mock Test 1 as a baseline, essay included.
- Note your estimated scores and the five weakest topics from the Progress tab.
## Week 1: number basics and Text Completion
- Quant: lessons and practice sets on number properties, fractions and decimals, and percents.
- Verbal: Text Completion lessons and practice sets (one, two and three blanks).
- Vocabulary: about 20 new flashcards a day, plus review.
- Essay: read the essay article; write one practice essay without a timer to learn the template.
## Week 2: algebra and Sentence Equivalence
- Quant: lessons and practice sets on linear equations, inequalities and exponents.
- Verbal: Sentence Equivalence lessons and practice sets.
- Read the time management article and start timing every practice set.
- Essay: one timed essay; rate it against the model essay.
- Weekend: take Mock Test 2.
## Week 3: word problems and reading
- Quant: word problems (rates, work, mixtures, ratios) and any algebra topic below 70%.
- Verbal: Reading Comprehension lessons and practice sets on short passages.
- Read the Quant tips article and practice plugging in and back-solving.
- Essay: one timed essay.
## Week 4: geometry, data and long reading
- Quant: geometry lessons and practice sets; data interpretation lessons and practice sets.
- Verbal: long passages and argument paragraphs.
- Read the Verbal tips article.
- Weekend: take Mock Test 3. Compare with Mock Test 1 topic by topic.
## Week 5: weak topics, round 1
- Pick the four weakest topics from the Progress tab and your error log.
- For each: reread the lesson, redo the practice set, read every explanation.
- Statistics and counting topics if not yet covered.
- Read the guessing and marking article; practice the two-pass method on every set.
- Essay: one timed essay.
- Weekend: take Mock Test 4.
## Week 6: mixed timed practice
- Mixed daily sets: one Verbal, one Quant, from different topics.
- Focus on section 1 accuracy: in each mock, review every section 1 error first.
- Essay: one timed essay, written in a new area (science, education, business) each time.
- Midweek: Mock Test 5. Weekend: Mock Test 6.
## Week 7: weak topics, round 2 and stamina
- Return to the topics that are still weak. If one has improved, replace it with the next one on the list.
- Read the test anxiety and stamina article and practice the breathing reset in mocks.
- Essay: one timed essay.
- Midweek: Mock Test 7. Weekend: Mock Test 8, at the same time of day as your real test.
## Week 8: final polish
- Days 1-3: reread your error log. Redo the five questions in it that taught you the most.
- Day 3: Mock Test 9, your last full mock.
- Days 4-6: light work only: flashcards, the essay template, a few explanations.
- Read the test day article and prepare your ID and route or room.
- Day before the test: rest. No new material.
## Checking progress
- After weeks 2, 4 and 6, compare your mock estimates and section 1 accuracy.
- If one measure is moving slowly, shift 30 minutes a day from the stronger measure to it.
- If you are ahead of your goal by week 6, use the extra time for harder sets in your strongest topics, to push section 2 into the harder level.
